preconditions.description: The number of computers n is between 1 and 1500 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(matrix) == n and all(len(row) == n for row in matrix)
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n lines, each with n integers representing the adjacency matrix.
The diagonal elements of the matrix are all 0.

preconditions.expression: all(matrix[i][j] == matrix[j][i] for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
all(matrix[i][j] > 0 for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n))
preconditions.description: All off-diagonal elements are strictly positive.

preconditions.expression: len(set(matrix[i][j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n))) == n * (n - 1) // 2
preconditions.description: All values a_{i,j} for i < j are distinct.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= x < 998244353 for x in results)
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a valid non-negative integer modulo 998244353.

postconditions.expression: all(results[k-1] == count_valid_partitions(n, matrix, k) % 998244353 for k in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: The k-th integer (1-indexed) equals the number of ways to partition the n computers into exactly k non-empty sets such that for any two pairs (s, f) and (x, y) where s, f, x are in the same set but x, y are in different sets, the condition a_{s,f} < a_{x,y} holds.
